annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is scam content because it promotes a cryptocurrency arbitrage method as an easy, repeatable 15% return in 10 minutes and directs viewers to purchase about $1,000 in crypto, transfer BNB between platforms, and exchange it for USDT. It also directs viewers toward a paid VIP channel, making the rapid-profit claim part of a concrete solicitation. The video includes a warning about scammers, and the records do not verify the platforms, prices, balances, transaction outcomes, or unclear password-sharing instruction.
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: The central offer links claimed arbitrage earnings to buying BNB, transferring it to another exchanger and exchanging BNB for USDT. The $1000 example is trading capital, while the claimed spread and reported profit are the promoted return. The description explicitly offers a subscription for purchase, and the speaker says the VIP channel provides additional private strategies and information. The purchase is for access to earning guidance, separate from the BNB trading capital.

evidence.observation: The description promises an easy 15% arbitrage profit in 10 minutes.
evidence.quote: In this video I will show you how easy it is to earn 15% profit on crypto arbitrage in 10 minutes.

evidence.observation: The description claims the strategy can be repeated without limit.
evidence.quote: You can use this strategy an unlimited number of times.

evidence.observation: The description supplies links labeled exchange and exchanger.
evidence.quote: Links from the video: Exchange: https://binance.com Exchanger: :https://bymirc.com/

evidence.observation: The speaker claims a nearly 15% cross-platform price difference and calls the spread earnings.
evidence.quote: make sure that BNB is more expensive there than on Binance. Right now, the difference is almost 15%. And this is the market spread, in other words, our earnings.

evidence.observation: The speaker instructs a market purchase using $1000 as an example; this is trading capital, not a guidance fee.
evidence.quote: Select Market and specify the amount of USDT. As an example, purchase $1000.

evidence.observation: The speaker instructs obtaining a BNB deposit address from the other site and entering it into a Binance withdrawal flow.
evidence.quote: Select BNB and click deposit Enter the amount of coins we bought earlier and Click get Address Copy the address Switch back to Binance Select BNB and then click withdrawal. Insert the address.

evidence.observation: The speaker describes a BNB-to-USDT exchange and a 0.1% exchange commission, distinct from a subscription price.
evidence.quote: Now let's exchange BNB and USDT the exchange commission is 0.1%.

evidence.observation: The speaker reports a $150 profit after claimed crediting; this is a reported result, not verified profit.
evidence.quote: The funds were successfully credited to our balance and at the same time the profit was $150

evidence.observation: The description offers a purchasable VIP-channel subscription through an administrator contact.
evidence.quote: If you still have questions or have a desire to purchase a subscription to the VIP channel, then write to the administrator Telegram channel - https://t.me/P2P_Whale

evidence.observation: The speaker identifies additional private strategies and information as the VIP channel's content.
evidence.quote: We also offer a VIP channel where you can find even more private strategies and insider information.

evidence.observation: The withdrawal narration contains an unclear password-related phrase; the recipient and intended action cannot be established reliably.
evidence.quote: Pass the password to the third person in the list which gives you the confirmation it is BNB.

evidence.observation: A Binance Withdraw Crypto form for BNB is displayed with an address field; the frame alone does not show a completed transfer.
A USDT withdrawal form on the other site is displayed with TRC20 selected and an amount entered; the frame alone does not show completion.
A Binance transaction-history page displays two USDT deposit entries marked Completed; the display does not independently verify the claimed profit.
